title: Who holds what: the PingOne session, its cookie and the tokens
lede: {{member}} signs in once. The PingOne session lives at PingOne and is recognised by a browser cookie. The apps hold tokens, which are a different thing with their own lifetime.

nodes.label: Browser
sub: HttpOnly: page scripts cannot read it

nodes.label: {{sensitiveApp}}
sub: mfa rule set by the admin

nodes.label: API
sub: checks token signature and expiry only

edges.label: revoke / timeout / mfa rule / flow report

steps.title: Sign in once
steps.what: {{member}} signs in through a DaVinci flow. Return Success Response creates the PingOne session and the browser receives a session cookie.
steps.why: The session is the signed-in state PingOne keeps. It is not a token.

steps.title: A second app, no prompt
steps.what: {{portalApp}} sends the browser to PingOne. The browser sends the cookie, PingOne recognises the session and issues tokens without asking for a password.
steps.why: That is single sign-on. The cookie is only for PingOne; it never goes to the app.

steps.title: Tokens are not the session
steps.what: {{portalApp}} calls the API with its access token. The API checks signature and expiry, not the session.
steps.why: Ending the session does not recall a token that was already issued. It lapses at expires_in.

steps.title: Step up
steps.what: {{sensitiveApp}} requires mfa signed on within a window the admin sets (Ping's write-up uses 8 or 9 hours; the lab starts at 8). Check Session looks at the mfa method's own last sign-on time; if mfa is missing or too old, the user is bounced to MFA. Completing MFA moves that time to now.
steps.why: Recording mfa only describes what the flow did. It never performs the challenge.

steps.title: The widget reuses the session
steps.what: {{embeddedApp}} POSTs the SDK-token request with the stored sessionToken in global.sessionToken. The flow checks the PingOne session and returns tokens.
steps.why: A GET cannot carry the body, and a dropped sessionToken means the flow shows its sign-in form again.

steps.title: An admin changes the session
steps.what: Deleting the session, shortening the idle timeout or raising the mfa rule changes what the next authorize returns. A flow that reports a method that never ran makes SSO sticky. Tokens the apps already hold keep working until they expire.
steps.why: The session and each token run on separate clocks. The cookie is only how the browser presents the session.
